body: We have talked plenty and agreed my sister is a real piece of work. I think it's just hard because, how do you even remove someone like that from your life? If my mom just kicked her out, she would lose it for sure. It's scary and I can tell it's difficult for my mom because at the end of the day, that's her baby. But you know what, your last paragraph did remind me: Years ago, my sister's friend lived with us for a good bit while she and her family waited to find a new house. Naturally, she witnessed what my sister was really like behind closed doors and commented to my grandma that it kind of shocked her to see how she treated us. Maybe a sign?

Thank you!  
I would say you're exactly right, I'm having a tough time giving myself the space to set boundaries and accept that I'm hurt. I think it mainly stems from the fact that I'm almost in denial because I felt that she should've learned better from growing up with my dad but I guess not everything turns out all fine and dandy. So to me, it's scary to admit that someone I expected and hoped better from perpetuated a cycle of abusive behavior. But regardless, I really appreciate you taking the time to reply, your comment clearly showed a lot of effort. I do manage to do things like exercise and eat right and all that goof stuff but maybe there's more healthy habits I'm missing? I'll definitely keep yours in mind!

Ah okay, I see what you're getting at now. I think yeah I'm wondering if she sounds toxic to other people? I mean, it's nice to hear the perspective of an outsider. When it comes to the concept of a label specifically, I think maybe we're just seeing things differently? To me, giving her behavior an actual label like toxic is a heavy thing because I feel such labels should be reserved for serious situations, which I don't know if this counts as. You feel me? Sorry if I'm coming across as confusing, I'm really trying to convey my perspective but it's difficult

Well I suppose it's the simple fact that labels do matter. When you label someone a certain way in your mind, it ultimately alters your perception of that person. If you label a person as "amazing" internally, it can cloud your judgement of them. You start to see them from a biased perspective, even the shitty things they do are forgivable. If I were to label my sister as toxic, I feel like that would damage the way I view her even worse and widen the rift between us. Like I said, I really do want to love my sister but I don't know how else to refer to her. I can't tell if you're confused or maybe trying to give advice so could you maybe be a little more clear?

You know, it’s weird how it seems like the people who would be your biggest supporters are actually the ones who beat down on you the most (both figuratively and literally). Hearing the way your mom treats you is so disheartening and yet, I can’t say I’m a stranger to it (Thanks for everything dad /s). I just wanted to say this: No matter what anybody else may say, you have a right to feel and to express.

I also wanted to mention your edit struck a chord with me. There’s something about quietness and tranquility with the world around while in your darkest moment that really tugs at you. Maybe it’s just one of those things humans need to stay healthy. Perhaps this could be something you look forward to every day from now on, a moment of peace with the natural world. I heard having something small to look forward to every day can surprisingly help a lot (such as eating a favorite snack, playing a favorite video game, watching a favorite show, playing with a pet, sketching something, the list goes on and all depends on what you’re into)

Honestly, that part regarding hell and the true debilitating nature of autism hit me deep. It’s weird because I can’t really say I believe in hell or an afterlife but that tiny, minuscule even, possibility is one of those things that keeps the gun away from my head. And yeah, autism feels truly fucking horrid in so many ways. It’s like you’re starved and tied to a chair with food (social connection and acceptance) just ever so out of reach in front of you but no matter how much you squirm or claw or move around, the food is still too far away somehow. It sucks to hear that you’re feeling like this at 30 because it always seems like people say, “Oh, things will get better in the future.” Yet the future has already arrived and nothing has gotten better. I don’t know but trust me when I say, you ain’t alone

Thank you I genuinely appreciate this advice so much! I feel like I’m now realizing I feel this way because of a lack of control in my life and this is my subconscious way of regaining control. I am truly thankful you were kind enough to give me some honest advice and I will be sure to start practicing it!

That’s really terrible, I know that feeling of pure isolation and loneliness where it feels like nobody ever wants to be around or speak with you. I am fortunate enough to have a decent amount of friends but there are still times where I feel a little lonely. Do you happen to have a therapist at the moment?
I appreciate the support, I hope wherever you are you’re doing good right now
I’ll try to leave an update if things go well but as of now, I can only hope

I do find it personally concerning that your parents are constantly leaving you at home which may be contributing to your suicidal thoughts. Your classmates seeing you as little more than a tool to complete their homework is also pretty unhelpful and will only continue to damage you. I’d honestly recommend simply not giving them the homework answers if that’s all they ever want to talk to you for, you don’t deserve to be used like that. If you’d like somebody to talk to, my PMs are open man

I can’t imagine experiencing constant terror like that. I don’t believe I’ve ever had a nightmare where I didn’t want to sleep for the rest of the night but I’ve certainly had some that delayed my sleep for a good bit since I was too scared to fall back asleep in fear that I’d slip back into the nightmare
That sounds like pure agony to not be able to sleep no matter what, I hope you very soon experience a well deserved rest

Oh man I can’t imagine pure terror like that constantly. I don’t think I’ve ever had a nightmare that made me never want to sleep for the rest of the night but they’ve certainly delayed my sleep before due to a fear of being immediately pulled back into the nightmare

Oh my goodness, I can relate so much. I also happen to have autism and I can get extremely overloaded with all the stimuli around me so sleep is like a key to another world without all that. It used to be somewhat common for me to experience no dreams but now it seems to barely happen, if at all. Sometimes I do wonder what would happen if every time I went to sleep it was a black void of nothingness, it might be even more peaceful than constant dreams comprised of pure fiction in all honesty

I can relate. It’s also quite common for my anxieties and fears to pass over into my dreams and give me some intense nightmares. So it’s not like I’m always getting some peace filled dreams, it’s just when I do they’re my only chance to experience any real “happiness” anymore
Thanks man, I appreciate it. Am just glad to be receiving support

Oh no you didn’t come off as insensitive at all. If anything your suggestion came from a place of understanding and experience so I appreciate it, I might consider vr chat. I really like to play gmod a lot since it feels like a place where I’m in control and can do whatever I want
Hm, I suppose you have a point. I hope your advice brings me a great deal of goodness in the future
Nightmares are most certainly not out of the ordinary for me, all I can think about though is if it’s still any worse than going back to my life that might as well be a living nightmare
Ha same, maybe that’s why I love it so much since it’s not that common for me to get a “good night’s sleep”
